title: ₱500 Office Exchange Gift Ideas (Philippines)
seoTitle: ₱500 Exchange Gift Ideas for Officemates | Christmas 2026
dek: Twenty practical gifts close to ₱500, grouped by your officemate's hobby: coffee, pickleball, tennis and running, music, gadgets and the desk.
teaser: Twenty practical gifts close to ₱500, grouped by your officemate's hobby.
description: Practical, hobby-based ₱500 exchange gift ideas for your office Christmas party: coffee, pickleball, running, earbuds, desk gadgets and more. Shop on Lazada.

hero.alt: AI sample render of an office gift-exchange table with kraft-wrapped gifts, red and terracotta ribbons, pine sprigs and warm string lights
hero.caption: AI sample render of a gift-exchange table, for illustration only. The real product photos from Lazada are below.

intro: It's monito-monita season again: names get drawn at the office, the budget is set, and you have a few weeks to find something your officemate will actually like.

₱500 is a realistic number. A 2018 YouGov survey found Filipino office workers were willing to spend about ₱500 on average for a Secret Santa gift, and that practical gifts were the most preferred. So every pick here is a useful gift close to that budget, grouped by hobby: find out what they're into, then jump to that section.

curation.title: Close to ₱500, matched to their hobby
summary: Gifting and career guides agree that the best office gifts match the person: find out what they enjoy outside work, then choose something practical within the group's budget. So we grouped this list by hobby and kept every pick close to ₱500, so nothing looks like an afterthought.
steps: Started from what officemates are into right now: coffee, pickleball, tennis and running, music and podcasts, gadgets, and long days at the desk.
Shortlisted well-reviewed listings close to ₱500 for each hobby, then narrowed them to 20.
Checked every product against Lazada's affiliate feed for price and stock on the day we published.
Said plainly on each card when a pick is a little over budget, unbranded, sold by a reseller or plugs into the wall.

sources.name: YouGov: Four in ten Filipino office workers will play Secret Santa
JobStreet PH: Last-minute gift ideas for your officemates and boss

callouts.title: How monito-monita works
callouts.body: Monito-monita (also called Kris Kringle) is the Filipino take on Secret Santa: names are drawn ahead of time, you keep your pick a secret, and the group agrees on a minimum and maximum price. Filipino groups often add fun theme categories to the exchange, so check if your office has one before you shop.

callouts.title: What to skip
callouts.body: Very personal gifts like perfume, cologne or pajamas, and gag gifts that could embarrass someone in front of the team. If you regift at all, it should be unopened, complete and in good condition, never a used item or an old corporate giveaway.

sellerNote: Prices move often, and some picks come in sizes or colours at different prices, so check the option you choose. A few picks are a little over or well under ₱500, and a few are sold by reseller shops rather than the brand's own store. We say so on each card.

tipGroups.title: Four tips for a gift that lands

tips.title: Find out their hobby
tips.body: Ask what they do outside work, or listen for hints at lunch and in the group chat. A gift that fits their hobby feels chosen, even at ₱500.

tips.title: Check the wish list first
tips.body: If your monito or monita posted a wish list, start there. No list? Listen for hints at work, check what they post about, or quietly ask a close officemate what they're into lately.

tips.title: Order early
tips.body: Order by mid-November so delivery doesn't squeeze your party date. Sale days like 11.11 can stretch the budget, too.

tips.title: Wrap it and add a name tag
tips.body: Wrap your gift before the party, even if it arrived in a nice box, and add a tag with your monito or monita's name so it doesn't get mixed up in the gift pile.

sections.name: For the coffee lover
sections.alt: AI sample render of a gift scene for the coffee lover, drawn from written descriptions of the picks below
sections.definition: Coffee lovers use their gear every day, so a good cup or grinder gets far more use than a novelty that ends up in a drawer. Most are ceramic, and each has a bit of personality, from a cat-face mug to a set that keeps coffee warm through long meetings.
sections.shoppingList: For the officemate who's never without a cup: café-style picks that stay on the desk all year.
tips: Not sure how they take their coffee? A cup, mug or warming set suits everyone from 3-in-1 fans to latte drinkers; save the grinder for someone who buys whole beans.
With unbranded ceramics, check the listing for a food-safe or lead-free note; the US FDA warns that some glazes can contain lead.
Wrap cups and mugs in a kitchen towel before the kraft paper, and if you have budget left, add a small pack of kapeng barako or drip bags.

items.label: Best for bean lovers
items.name: Quencha 150 g manual coffee bean grinder
items.verdict: A neat hand-crank grinder from Quencha's own store, for the officemate who buys whole beans and wants a fresher cup.
items.summary: Quencha is a house brand of home-goods company Sunbeams Lifestyle, and this listing comes from its own store. The slim hand-crank grinder holds 150 g of beans, adjusts from fine to coarse and comes in four muted colours that look good on a desk.

reviewers.point: Quencha is one of Sunbeams Lifestyle's own brands. Its brand page lists a 150 g capacity, fine-to-coarse adjustment, stainless steel grinding parts and removable parts for cleaning.
The National Coffee Association recommends grinding beans as close to brewing time as possible, and a coarse, rock-salt-sized grind for French press.
reviewers.source: National Coffee Association (About Coffee): French press coffee

reviewers.point: Common-sense care: brush out leftover grounds after each use, and let any washed parts dry fully before grinding again.

pros: Sold by the brand's own store (Sunbeams Lifestyle)
Fine-to-coarse adjustment for drip, pour-over or press
Four colours: Snow, Sand, Stone and Onyx
cons: Hand-cranked, so grinding takes a bit of arm work
Body material and number of settings not stated
items.bestFor: The officemate who buys whole beans or brews with a French press or pour-over
items.tip: Snow or Sand gives a soft, neutral desk look; Onyx suits someone who likes black. Add a small pack of whole beans to finish the gift.

items.label: Best cup and saucer
items.name: Japanese-style stone-texture ceramic cup and saucer
items.verdict: A cup and saucer with a sandy, stone-like matte finish that makes a desk coffee feel like a café order. The 280 ml size suits most.
items.summary: This unbranded cup is round and slightly egg-shaped, with a stone-like textured matte glaze, and sits on a wide matching saucer. The listing name offers 110 ml and 280 ml sizes in black or white; the bigger cup suits everyday coffee and milky drinks.

reviewers.point: A traditional cappuccino is served in a 150–180 ml cup, so the 110 ml size is better for short, strong drinks, while 280 ml fits a regular coffee or a milky one.
A cup with a matching saucer is treated as more formal than a mug, which is why this set feels like a step up from the usual office mug.
Common-sense care: hand-wash and dry it soon after use so coffee rings don't settle into the matte, textured glaze.

pros: Stone-like matte texture looks handmade and grown-up
Comes with a wide matching saucer
Two sizes and two colours to choose from
cons: Unbranded; maker and glaze details not given
Matte texture can hold coffee stains if left unwashed
items.bestFor: The officemate who orders flat whites and likes a calm, minimalist desk
items.tip: Choose 280 ml unless they mostly drink espresso. Black matches the photo; white is softer. Wrap cup and saucer separately so they don't chip.

items.label: Cutest desk mug
items.name: Black cat-shaped ceramic mug, 380 ml
items.verdict: A glossy black mug with cat ears on the rim and sleepy white eyes: cute enough to make them smile, tidy enough for a work desk.
items.summary: This unbranded ceramic mug is shaped like a round cat's head, with two small pointed ears rising from the rim and simple white half-closed eyes. At 380 ml it holds a bit more than a standard mug, good for a big morning coffee. The price is for one mug.

reviewers.point: A typical mug holds about 250–350 ml, so at 380 ml this one is on the roomy side.
Common-sense care: the pointed ear tips on the rim are the most chip-prone spot, so hand-wash it and don't stack other mugs inside.

pros: Playful cat shape without loud prints or text
Roomy 380 ml for a big morning coffee
Glossy glaze is easy to wipe clean
cons: Unbranded, and the listing gives no care info
Price is for one mug, though the photo shows two
items.bestFor: The cat lover, or the officemate whose desk is full of cute stationery
items.tip: Only black is shown in the listing photo. Tuck a few coffee sachets inside, then wrap it in a kitchen towel so the ear tips don't chip.

items.label: For the anime fan
items.name: One Piece Luffy straw-hat ceramic cup and saucer
items.verdict: A fun straw-hat cup for the officemate who never misses an episode. It's from an unbranded shop and a little over ₱500.
items.summary: Set upside down on its brim-shaped saucer, this ceramic cup looks like Luffy's red-banded straw hat, so it doubles as a desk display. It is from an unbranded shop, isn't listed as official merchandise, and was a little over ₱500 at our last check.

reviewers.point: Luffy is best known for his red-ribboned straw hat, the design this cup and saucer recreate.
The US FDA notes lead is often used with bright red, orange and yellow decorations, so for an unbranded cup like this, look for a lead-free or food-safe note before daily use.
reviewers.source: US FDA: Questions and Answers on Lead-Glazed Traditional Pottery

reviewers.point: Common-sense care: hand-wash it; the raised hat band and wide brim chip more easily than a plain mug.

pros: Instantly recognisable straw-hat design
Doubles as a desk or shelf display piece
Ceramic cup with a matching brim saucer
cons: A little over ₱500 at our last check
Unbranded shop; not listed as official merchandise
items.bestFor: The officemate who is a big fan of the series
items.tip: The photo shows three hat designs; make sure the straw hat (the one named in the listing) is the variant you order. Hand-washing is safest.

items.label: Under budget: add a treat
items.name: Warming mug gift set with 55°C heated coaster
items.verdict: A boxed mug, lid, spoon and warming coaster that stops desk coffee from going cold, with plenty of budget left for a treat.
items.summary: This unbranded set comes in a gift box with a ribbon handle: a white ceramic mug with lid, a gold-tone spoon and a warming coaster that the listing says holds drinks at a constant 55°C. At well under ₱500, you can add beans, drip bags or a pastry.

reviewers.point: A 2022 Scientific Reports study found black coffee was best liked at about 58–66°C, so a 55°C coaster keeps a cup warm and sippable rather than piping hot.
reviewers.source: Ristenpart et al., Scientific Reports (2022), via PubMed Central

reviewers.point: The DTI's Bureau of Philippine Standards tells shoppers to look for a PS mark or ICC sticker on products under mandatory certification, and to verify ICC stickers with its mobile app.
reviewers.source: DTI Bureau of Philippine Standards: PS and ICC Marks

reviewers.point: Common-sense care: switch the coaster off when you leave your desk, keep it dry, and wipe it clean instead of washing it.

pros: Gift box with ribbon handle, ready to give
Keeps coffee warm through long meetings
Leaves budget for beans, drip bags or a snack
cons: Power type (USB or wall plug) isn't shown in the photo
Unbranded electrical item: look for a PS mark or ICC sticker
items.bestFor: The officemate whose coffee always goes cold during meetings
items.tip: Check the listing or ask the seller if it's USB or wall-plug powered, and look for a PS mark or ICC sticker. Then add a small coffee treat.

sections.name: For the pickleball, tennis and running crowd
sections.alt: AI sample render of a gift scene for the pickleball, tennis and running crowd, drawn from written descriptions of the picks below
sections.definition: Sporty officemates wear out their gear fast, so fresh balls, a better paddle bag or a running belt gets used within the week instead of sitting in a drawer. Match the gift to the sport they actually play and stick to trusted sports brands, and it lands every time.
sections.shoppingList: For the officemate who plays pickleball after work, swings a racket on weekends or runs before sunrise.
tips: Ask a teammate which sport they play first, and for pickleball, whether they play mostly on outdoor or indoor courts.
Keep ball cans and packs sealed and wrap them as they are. Tennis balls start losing bounce once the can is opened.
Branded gear sold by resellers can vary, so check each listing's authenticity details and return policy before you check out.

items.label: Best pickleball gift
items.name: LI-NING PZ40 outdoor pickleball balls, 3-pack
items.verdict: A gift a regular player will actually use up: three outdoor-style balls from Li-Ning's own store, made for open-air courts.
items.summary: Pickleball balls crack and lose their bounce with steady play, so a fresh pack is always welcome. This Li-Ning 3-pack is the 40-hole outdoor style, rotomolded per the listing, and sold by LINING Official Store on Lazada.

reviewers.point: Outdoor pickleballs usually have more holes, close to the 40 maximum, and are harder and heavier than indoor balls, which helps them fly straighter in the wind.
Rotomolded balls are formed as a single piece of plastic in a mould, not two halves welded together; the faint seam line is just where the mould parts.
USA Pickleball allows 26 to 40 holes, and sanctioned tournaments must use a ball from its approved list. We couldn't confirm this pack is on that list, so treat it as a rec and practice ball.

pros: Sold by Li-Ning's official store on Lazada
40-hole outdoor design for open-air courts
Bright orange ball is easy to track (per photo)
cons: Stock was low at our last check
Not confirmed as tournament-approved
items.bestFor: The officemate who plays pickleball on outdoor courts after work or on weekends
items.tip: Outdoor balls suit open-air courts. If they mostly play indoors in a gym, ask a teammate first, and order early since stock was low.

items.label: Most stylish carry
items.name: RGFV waterproof pickleball crossbody bag
items.verdict: A sporty crossbody that carries paddles to the court and protects them on the way, in a clean white perforated finish.
items.summary: Paddles get scuffed tossed loose in a tote or the back seat. This zip-around case holds two paddles (as shown in the photo), with a front zip pocket and an adjustable crossbody strap. RGFV is a little-known brand, sold by a general shop.

reviewers.point: Paddle maker Selkirk recommends a paddle cover as a shield against scratches, scrapes and accidental damage, and says to store paddles in a dry, room-temperature space.
Onix advises against leaving paddles, balls and gear bags in a hot vehicle for long, since heat can affect paddle materials and ball performance; keep gear somewhere cool and shaded.
reviewers.source: Onix Pickleball, playing in hot weather

reviewers.point: Common-sense care: wipe the bag with a damp cloth and let it air-dry open after a sweaty game before zipping the paddles back in.

pros: Holds two paddles, as shown in the photo
Adjustable crossbody strap keeps hands free
Front zip pocket for keys and cards
cons: Little-known brand, sold by a general shop
Paddles likely not included; fabric not named
items.bestFor: The officemate who brings a paddle (or two) to the court every week
items.tip: White shows court dust, so it suits someone who keeps their gear neat. If they use an extra-long paddle, check the bag size in the listing first.

items.label: Best for tennis players
items.name: Slazenger Wimbledon Ultra-Vis tennis balls, 1 can
items.verdict: The Wimbledon ball in a sealed can: a classic, useful gift a tennis-loving officemate will be glad to crack open on court.
items.summary: Slazenger has supplied Wimbledon's balls since 1902, and this is its Wimbledon Ultra-Vis ball, one sealed can of three per the photo. It's sold by MVLSPORTS, a sports shop reselling the brand, not Slazenger's own store.

reviewers.point: Slazenger became the official tennis ball supplier to Wimbledon in 1902, which Wikipedia calls the longest unbroken sporting sponsorship in history; its ball production is now based in the Philippines.
Slazenger says the Wimbledon ball uses a fine-wool woven cloth, an Ultra Vis dye for visibility, and Hydroguard treatment that repels up to 70% more water than a standard ball.
Pressurised tennis balls start losing their bounce once the can is opened; the sealed can keeps the pressure inside the balls until first use.

pros: Wimbledon's official ball brand since 1902
Sealed can keeps the balls fresh until opened
Water-repelling Hydroguard cloth, per Slazenger
cons: Sold by a reseller, not Slazenger's own store
Only 3 balls; regular players use them up fast
items.bestFor: The officemate who plays tennis on weekends or stays up for Wimbledon every July
items.tip: Keep the can sealed until the party, since balls start losing bounce once it's opened. A ribbon around the tin is all the wrapping it needs.

items.label: Best for any sport
items.name: adidas sweat-absorbing sports headband
items.verdict: A slim headband that keeps sweat and stray hair out of their eyes for tennis, pickleball or a run. Check the listing's authenticity first.
items.summary: A slim black adidas headband for sweaty games and runs, shown with a small silver logo. The seller, Brand Super Deal, is a reseller and not adidas's own store, so check the listing's authenticity details before you buy.

reviewers.point: Headbands are worn around the forehead during physical activity to absorb sweat, which helps keep it out of the eyes.
The Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines (IPOPHL) tells online shoppers to check the '5Ps' before buying branded goods: packaging, price, product, promotional message and place.
Common-sense care: hand wash in cool water with mild soap and air-dry, skipping the dryer so the elastic keeps its stretch.

pros: Works for tennis, pickleball, running and the gym
Slim black band goes with any outfit or kit
Small and light, easy to wrap
cons: Sold by a reseller, not adidas's own store
Pack count and size aren't stated in the name
items.bestFor: The sporty officemate who sweats through every game, whatever the sport
items.tip: Before buying, read the listing's authenticity details and return policy, and compare the photos with adidas's own product photos.

items.label: Best for runners
items.name: Decathlon KIPRUN Basic 2 smartphone running belt
items.verdict: A light, flat running belt from Decathlon's own store that holds a big phone and keys, so their hands stay free on every run.
items.summary: No runner likes a phone bouncing in a pocket. Decathlon's KIPRUN Basic 2 sits on the hips, fits waists from 40 to 95 cm, and holds a large phone with a separate key pocket and an earphone opening. Sold by Decathlon's own store.

reviewers.point: Decathlon lists a one-size adjustable strap for waists from 40 to 95 cm, a 245 x 100 mm main pocket for large phones, a small inner key compartment so keys don't scratch the phone, and a weight of 75 g.
Decathlon says to wear it on the hips over a layer of clothing, at the front or back; care is hand wash at up to 40°C, with no tumble drying or ironing.

pros: Sold by Decathlon's own store on Lazada
Holds a large phone plus keys, per Decathlon
Just 75 g, with an earphone opening
cons: Fits waists up to 95 cm only
No room for a water bottle
items.bestFor: The officemate training for a fun run, or who jogs or walks before work
items.tip: This listing is black, the safest pick for any running kit. It fits waists from 40 to 95 cm, so it suits most officemates.

sections.name: For the music and podcast listener
sections.alt: AI sample render of a gift scene for the music and podcast listener, drawn from written descriptions of the picks below
sections.definition: Earbuds get used every day, on the commute, at the desk and on a lunch-break walk, so they're a gift your monito or monita won't leave in a drawer. At this price you're buying budget earbuds, so we kept to named brands and spell out what each listing does and doesn't promise.
sections.shoppingList: Wireless earbuds near ₱500 for the officemate who always has a playlist or podcast going.
tips: "Noise cancelling" on cheap earbuds often means ENC, which cleans up your voice on calls. Only ANC quiets what you hear.
Pick open-ear hooks for runners and anyone who needs to hear the office; in-ear buds give more bass on a noisy commute.
Charge the case fully before wrapping, and use a phone charger that has a PS mark or ICC sticker.

items.label: Easy everyday buds
items.name: OTN Wireless Earbuds with LED Display Case
items.verdict: Cream stem-style buds with a handy battery display on the case. Easy to like, as long as you don't expect a silent bubble.
items.summary: A small-brand pair in soft cream, with AirPods-style stems and a case whose digital display shows the charge, per the photo. The listing promises noise cancelling, Hi-Fi audio and long battery life but gives no hours or ANC details.

reviewers.point: "Noise cancelling" can mean two different things. ANC uses mics and anti-noise to quiet what you hear; ENC only cleans up your voice for the person on the call. This listing doesn't say which one it uses.
reviewers.source: SlashGear: ANC vs ENC noise cancellation, explained

reviewers.point: The listing also calls this an open-ear design. Open styles let outside sound in on purpose (soundcore rates their noise isolation as low), so don't expect them to shut out a noisy jeepney ride.
reviewers.source: soundcore: Open-ear vs in-ear vs over-ear headphones

reviewers.point: Common-sense care: wipe the buds and the charging contacts in the case with a dry cloth now and then so they keep charging properly.

pros: Battery display on the case shows the charge at a glance
Soft cream colour looks neat on any desk
Tip-free stem style, easy to pop in and out
cons: Noise-cancelling type and battery hours aren't stated
Small brand; we couldn't find a brand website
items.bestFor: The officemate who plays podcasts at the desk or on the commute
items.tip: Only cream shows in the listing photo, so check the colour menu at checkout. Charge the case fully before you wrap it.

items.label: Bluetooth 6.0 pick
items.name: Jeep EW138 Wireless Earbuds (Bluetooth 6.0)
items.verdict: Cream-and-brown buds carrying the Jeep name and Bluetooth 6.0, per the listing. A good-looking gift for the outdoorsy officemate.
items.summary: Stemless cream earbuds in a rounded case with a chocolate-brown inside, per the photo. The listing names Bluetooth 6.0, touch controls and a mic. Jeep's owner licenses the name for lifestyle goods; we couldn't confirm who makes these.

reviewers.point: Licensing International's 2025 awards credit Stellantis, Jeep's owner, and agency IMG with a global Jeep lifestyle programme covering apparel, footwear, bags, e-mobility and more. We couldn't confirm which licensed company makes these earbuds, so judge them as budget buds.
reviewers.source: Licensing International: Best Brand, Corporate 2025 (Jeep, Stellantis/IMG)

reviewers.point: Bluetooth 6.0's headline addition is Channel Sounding, a secure way for two devices to measure the distance between them. A newer version number doesn't by itself mean better sound.
reviewers.source: Bluetooth SIG: Bluetooth Core 6.0 feature overview

reviewers.point: Common-sense care: the listing doesn't claim any water resistance, so keep them out of the rain and wipe off sweat after use.

pros: Bluetooth 6.0, the newest version, per the listing
Warm cream-and-brown look, not plain white
Touch controls and a mic for calls, per the listing
cons: We couldn't confirm the maker behind the Jeep name
No battery hours or water resistance stated
items.bestFor: The outdoorsy or car-loving officemate who wants simple daily buds
items.tip: Only the cream-and-brown version shows in the listing photo, so check the colour menu before checkout.

facts.v: Stemless buds, cream and brown case

items.label: Familiar tech brand
items.name: Lenovo thinkplus LP19 Wireless Earbuds
items.verdict: A familiar tech name for under ₱500, in black or white. It's sold by a reseller, not Lenovo's own store, so check it when it arrives.
items.summary: From Lenovo's budget thinkplus range, sold here by FORSINING & Lenovo Store, a reseller rather than Lenovo itself. The listing names Bluetooth 5.1 and dual HD mics; the photo shows round pebble cases in black and white.

reviewers.point: Notebookcheck describes a sibling model, the thinkplus LP70 Pro, as budget Lenovo earbuds launched in China with no global launch announced. We couldn't find a Lenovo spec page for the LP19 itself.
reviewers.source: Notebookcheck: Lenovo ThinkPlus LP70 Pro budget earbuds

reviewers.point: "Dual HD microphones" are about how you sound on calls. Mic-side noise reduction (ENC) helps the other person hear you but doesn't quiet the room for you; that's ANC, which this listing doesn't claim.
reviewers.source: SlashGear: ANC vs ENC noise cancellation, explained

reviewers.point: Common-sense check: when it arrives, make sure the box and case say thinkplus LP19 and that both buds pair with your phone before you wrap it.

pros: Big tech brand name at around ₱500
Black or white, per the listing photo
Dual mics for calls, per the listing
cons: Sold by a reseller, not Lenovo's own store
No Lenovo spec page for battery or water resistance
items.bestFor: The officemate who trusts big tech names and takes lots of calls
items.tip: Pick black if they're hard on gadgets, since it hides scuffs, or white for a clean desk look. Test that both buds pair before wrapping.

items.label: Best for runners
items.name: MIXTONE Open-Ear Hook Wireless Earphones
items.verdict: Open-ear hooks that keep you hearing the world on a run or at your desk. A little over ₱500, but the most distinctive pair here.
items.summary: Ear-hook earphones that sit outside the ear canal instead of plugging it, per the listing, with bright orange hooks, chrome pods and a round case with a digital display. Sold by the MIXTONE brand store. Nice for runners and desk-bound listeners.

reviewers.point: Open-ear designs let you hear traffic, or colleagues in an office, while you listen. The trade-offs are moderate bass compared with sealed earbuds and a slight sound leak in very quiet rooms.
reviewers.source: Shokz: Can open-ear headphones really deliver comfort and quality?

reviewers.point: Because open-ear styles rest gently on the ear rather than sealing it, they're easy to wear for hours, but they block little outside noise.
reviewers.source: soundcore: Open-ear vs in-ear vs over-ear headphones

reviewers.point: Common-sense care: the listing says water resistant but gives no IP rating, so wipe off sweat after workouts and keep them out of heavy rain.

pros: Open-ear, so you still hear traffic and officemates
Ear hooks give a steadier fit on runs and gym days
Bold orange-and-chrome look, per the photo
cons: A little over ₱500 at our last check
Less bass and more sound leak than in-ear buds
items.bestFor: Runners, gym-goers and anyone who needs to hear the office while listening
items.tip: Only the orange-and-chrome version shows in the listing photo, so check the colour menu. Charge the case fully before wrapping.

facts.v: Resistant per listing, no IP rating

sections.name: For the gadget person
sections.alt: AI sample render of a gift scene for the gadget person, drawn from written descriptions of the picks below
sections.definition: Gadget lovers enjoy small tech that fixes an everyday annoyance or makes their hobby easier, and both of these do exactly that. Match the gift to their habits: the one who is always hunting for keys, or the one who is always filming.
sections.shoppingList: Clever little tech they will actually use, from finding lost keys to filming hands-free.
tips: Check their phone first: the BAVIN tracker tag is for iPhone users, per the listing. Not sure? The tripod is the safer pick, since it simply clamps the phone.
Charge rechargeable gadgets before wrapping and tuck in a short how-to note, so they can try it right at the party.
Keep the order screenshot: both listings advertise a warranty, and proof of purchase makes any claim easier.

items.label: Best for iPhone users
items.name: BAVIN TAG01 Bluetooth tracker tag for iPhone
items.verdict: A neat key-finder for the officemate who is always asking where their keys went, as long as they use an iPhone.
items.summary: A small white Bluetooth tag that shows up in Apple's Find My app, so they can locate keys, a bag or even a pet's collar from their iPhone. The listing photo shows a steel-wire key loop and a free silicone case, and it ships from BAVIN's own store.

reviewers.point: Apple says adding an AirTag or a Find My network accessory needs an iPhone or iPad on iOS or iPadOS 14.5 or later; you follow the maker's instructions, then add it in the Find My app.
reviewers.source: Apple Support: How to add an AirTag to Find My

reviewers.point: Tags like this have no GPS of their own. Apple explains that nearby iPhones, iPads and Macs securely and anonymously send a lost item's location to iCloud, so updates depend on Apple devices passing by.

The photo badge says "Find My Device", the old name of Google's Android finder (now Find Hub), but the listing name says the tag is for iPhone users. If your officemate uses Android, check with the seller first.
reviewers.source: Google blog: Find Hub on Android

pros: Find keys, bags or wallets from an iPhone
Silicone case included as a free gift (per photo)
Sold by BAVIN's own brand store
cons: For iPhone users only, per the listing
Not GPS: location updates rely on Apple devices nearby
items.bestFor: The iPhone user who is forever misplacing keys, bags or a work ID
items.tip: Quietly confirm they use an iPhone before you buy. It comes in white; slip it onto a keyring inside the gift box so it is ready to pair.

items.label: Best for content creators
items.name: MODOFO face-tracking selfie stick tripod with remote
items.verdict: For the officemate who films everything: it stands on its own and turns to keep their face in frame.
items.summary: A selfie stick that opens into a free-standing tripod, with a motorised head that rotates 360° to follow a face, per the listing. Great for cooking clips, live selling, dance videos or video calls, with a remote for hands-free shots.

reviewers.point: Selfie sticks are banned at some museums, theme parks, concerts and stadiums for safety and recording reasons, so a quick check before a trip or event saves a hassle at the gate.
Common sense: face tracking relies on the head's small camera seeing a face, so it follows best in good light and at a moderate distance. Charge it fully before wrapping so it works out of the box.

pros: Turns 360° to keep a face in frame (per listing)
Selfie stick and free-standing tripod in one
Remote control for hands-free shots
cons: Lesser-known brand; few details beyond the listing
Fill lights in the photo may depend on the option
items.bestFor: The officemate who vlogs, live-sells or shoots TikToks after work
items.tip: The photo shows twin round fill lights beside the phone; check that the option you pick includes them before checking out.

sections.name: For the desk-bound officemate
sections.alt: AI sample render of a gift scene for the desk-bound officemate, drawn from written descriptions of the picks below
sections.definition: Officemates who spend the whole day at one desk appreciate anything that makes that small space cooler, calmer or cosier. Mini fans and glowing diffusers are compact, run on USB or a rechargeable battery, and get used every single workday.
sections.shoppingList: Small comforts for long hours at the workstation: a cool breeze, a soft glow and a little mist.
tips: Mini fans are the safest bet: almost everyone gets warm at their desk, and battery fans keep going on the commute and during brownouts.
With diffusers, think of the seatmates: plain water or a light scent is kinder in a shared office, and distilled water helps avoid white dust.
Two picks are a little over ₱500. If your group is strict, the TYLEX fan and the flame diffuser were under ₱500 at our last check.

items.label: Most useful 3-in-1
items.name: JISULIFE 3-in-1 mini fan, power bank and flashlight
items.verdict: A cute folding fan that also tops up a phone and lights the way: a lifesaver for hot commutes and brownouts.
items.summary: Three gadgets in one pocket-size capsule: a folding handheld fan, a power bank that can top up a phone in a pinch, and a small flashlight. The listing calls it 4800mAh, and the photo shows pastel pink, white, navy and brown versions with little bear ears.

reviewers.point: JISULIFE's own site lists the basic Handheld Fan 8 (F8) at 2000mAh with 2 speeds, USB-C charging and a flashlight. This listing says 4800mAh with model F8 in the photo, so check the box for the exact version.
The bigger Handheld Fan 8 Plus is listed at 4500mAh with 3 speeds. JISULIFE's 12-month warranty is stated for orders from its own store; NeatPH is a reseller, so ask the seller about warranty cover.
reviewers.source: JISULIFE official store: Handheld Fan 8 Plus

pros: Fan, power bank and flashlight in one
Folds small enough for a pocket or bag
Cute bear-ear design in four colours
cons: A little over ₱500 at our last check
Sold by a reseller (NeatPH), not JISULIFE's own store
items.bestFor: The officemate with a long commute who always runs hot
items.tip: Pick the colour at checkout: pink or white feels sweet, navy or brown suits a low-key officemate. Charge it and pack the cable in the box.

items.label: Best wear-anywhere fan
items.name: TYLEX XM25 wearable mini fan
items.verdict: A flat, pastel mini fan they can hold, hang around the neck, strap to a wrist or stand on the desk.
items.summary: A slim, palm-size fan from Manila gadget brand TYLEX that works five ways, per the listing: handheld, around the neck, on the wrist, at the waist or standing on a desk. The photo shows three speeds and soft sage green, blush pink and off-white colours.

reviewers.point: TYLEX is a Manila-based gadget brand. Its own website lists the XM25 in its neck-fan range alongside chargers and power banks, and mentions a local warranty policy.
ProductNation PH's portable-fan roundup ranked a sibling TYLEX mini fan, the XM35, as its best overall pick. The XM25 itself was not part of that roundup.
Common sense: dust builds up quickly on small fan grilles, so wipe it with a dry cloth or soft brush every so often.

pros: Hold it, wear it or stand it on the desk
Sold by TYLEX's own official store
Three speeds, per the listing photo
cons: Battery size and runtime are not stated
A personal breeze, not a room cooler
items.bestFor: The officemate who moves between desk, meetings and a hot commute
items.tip: Choose a colour at checkout: sage green and off-white look clean on any desk, pink is the sweeter pick. Charge it before wrapping.

items.label: Most eye-catching
items.name: Flame-effect USB aroma diffuser
items.verdict: A little desk show: cool mist lit up so it looks like a dancing flame, with no fire and no heat.
items.summary: A compact ultrasonic diffuser whose mist is lit from below so it looks like a flickering flame, orange on the white version and purple on the black one in the photo. It runs on USB and can be used with water alone or a few drops of essential oil.

reviewers.point: The US EPA notes that ultrasonic humidifiers spread the minerals in tap water into the air, sometimes as white dust, and recommends distilled water. It also advises emptying, drying and refilling portable units daily.
reviewers.source: US EPA: Use and care of home humidifiers

reviewers.point: This is an unbranded plug-in gadget. DTI says the PS mark and ICC sticker are the consumer's assurance of certified quality and safety, so look for one on the box and keep the packaging.
reviewers.source: DTI Bureau of Philippine Standards: PS and ICC marks

reviewers.point: Common sense: scents carry in a shared office, so run it with plain water or a light scent, and switch it off before leaving for the day.

pros: Mist lit up like a flickering flame
USB powered and compact for a desk
Works with water alone or a drop of oil
cons: Unbranded; the seller's store name does not show
Needs regular emptying and cleaning
items.bestFor: The officemate who loves a cosy, calming corner at their desk
items.tip: White suits a light desk and black looks dramatic with the purple flame. Wrap a small bottle of distilled water with it as a thoughtful extra.

items.label: Slightly over budget
items.name: KINSCOTER candle-light mini aroma diffuser
items.verdict: A tiny lantern for the desk: a warm candle-like glow and a soft wisp of mist, with no open flame.
items.summary: A mini diffuser that looks like a little lantern: a matte black base under a smoky clear dome, with a glowing amber core like an old filament bulb. It puffs cool mist from the top, doubles as a soft night light and runs on USB, per the listing.

reviewers.point: The US EPA notes that ultrasonic humidifiers can spread minerals from tap water as white dust and recommends distilled water, plus emptying and refilling portable units daily.
reviewers.source: US EPA: Use and care of home humidifiers

reviewers.point: This is a little-known brand sold by a reseller. DTI says the PS mark and ICC sticker show certified quality and safety, so check the box for one and keep the packaging.
reviewers.source: DTI Bureau of Philippine Standards: PS and ICC marks

reviewers.point: Common sense: set it on a flat spot away from papers and the keyboard so a knock or spill does not reach the laptop.

pros: Warm candle-like glow with no open flame
Doubles as a soft night light
Small and USB powered for a desk
cons: Slightly over ₱500 at our last check
Sold by a reseller, not a KINSCOTER store
items.bestFor: The officemate who likes a calm, softly lit desk on late shifts
items.tip: It runs on USB, so it can draw power from a laptop or phone charger; check whether an adapter is included. Add a small bottle of distilled water.
